title: Choose the visual world for The Tooth Care, safer hand
question: You asked for directions an everyday visitor will recognise. Three familiar grounded worlds, plus the category standard played straight. You pick; nothing is pre-assigned.

options.label: The Family Album
options.lineage: Dhaka photo-studio prints and the family album with hand-written captions, kept for decades
options.thesis: Big, warm photographs of Dr. Uzzal with his patients carry the whole page; the words are captions.
options.viewport: A full-width candid photo of Dr. Uzzal mid-conversation with a patient, a short caption in his words underneath, name and both chambers printed small, and one coral button: Message Dr. Uzzal on WhatsApp. Reviews appear as captioned snapshots, 'Rahim, patient since 2021' style once consent exists.
options.risk: Lives or dies on real photography. Until the clinic supplies candid photos it is a page of labelled frames. Structurally the closest to what visitors already expect.

options.label: The Illustrated Storybook
options.lineage: Boi Mela paperback covers: flat brushed colour fields, friendly hand-drawn illustration, clear lettering
options.thesis: A calm, illustrated page that explains dentistry the way a good children's book explains anything: one idea per spread, no fear.
materials: navy line illustration with soft fills
options.viewport: A soft colour field with a simple line illustration of the doctor and a patient talking across a desk (no chair, no drill), the headline in his words, a short sentence, and one warm button. Each section below is a 'spread' with its own small illustration: how the first visit goes, what patients say, where to find me.
options.risk: Needs a consistent illustration set drawn in one hand; stock-style vector people would sink it. Reads friendly and safe, and is the most common 'approachable clinic' rendition.

options.label: The Conversation
options.lineage: The messaging thread every Dhaka phone user reads daily
options.thesis: The home page is the first chat with Dr. Uzzal: your questions on the right, his answers on the left, and the real WhatsApp button at the end.
materials: green only on the real WhatsApp action
options.viewport: His photo and name as the chat header, then the first exchange: 'Will it hurt?' answered in his words, 'What does the first visit cost?' answered honestly, then the green button to continue the conversation for real. Sections below are further exchanges: patients' words, locations, services.
options.risk: Can be mistaken for a chatbot, which the brand rejects; it must read as a written conversation, never an interactive one. Long pages of bubbles tire the eye on desktop.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The modern clinic site every good competitor ships, executed at full craft with Dr. Uzzal's voice and real facts inside it.
canonCard.viewport: Header with logo and phone, a hero with a large photo, a warm headline, trust line (4.8 on Google, two branches), and a blue Message on WhatsApp button; then services in a grid, reviews, doctor bio, locations with maps, footer. When chosen, you name two or three clinic sites it should sit alongside and their craft becomes the bar.
canonCard.risk: Familiar by design; it earns trust through polish and real content, not through distinctiveness.
